description: Save slots around the village-state save (Features WV1, P1.core-slots; catalog saves-slots-autosave; ruling U83(1)): deleting a slot and what the slot list and the Continue target become; autosave at an interval with its indicator ("Saving…", "Saved!", "Save failed"); quick save on F5 and quick load on F9 (core's KeyboardMap), including F9 with an empty or corrupted quick slot and a game with no quick slot. The session does no I/O: each step returns the effect the host performs (write, read, remove) and the host reports it with a finished step. Runner: src/save-slots-corpus.ts (ops config, continue, rows, indicator, run). Numbers compare within tolerance; everything else exactly, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent). A non-finite number is written as null in an input. Regenerate with npm run save-slots-corpus; npm run save-slots-corpus:check fails on any difference.
sources: Rules new in core (src/save-slots.ts, src/ui/save-indicator-model.ts), from the original game: babylon origin/main WorldStateManager (MAX_SAVE_SLOTS 3, AUTO_SAVE_INTERVAL_MS 5 min, deleteSlot), SaveIndicator (hold 1000 ms, fade 2000 ms, "Saved!" / "Save failed"), GameMenuSystem (one save, load or delete at a time; "No save data"), MainMenuScreen (Continue is the most recent); core KeyboardMap KEY_QUICK_SAVE F5 / KEY_QUICK_LOAD F9 ("slot 0").
Inputs are synthetic; every expected is core's answer, and src/conformance/__tests__/save-slots.test.ts pins the same rules independently.

slotMessages.invalid_format: Unrecognized save format — this slot cannot be loaded.
slotMessages.missing_save_file: Save data is missing or unreadable.
slotMessages.integrity_mismatch: Save file integrity check failed — file may be corrupted or tampered.

contract.continueRule: the loadable (ok) slot with the latest summary.savedAt (Date.parse of an ISO time: an instant, its zone offset applied with its sign, so the same instant written two ways is a tie); a tie goes to the lowest index; an unreadable or missing time is older than any readable one; no loadable slot: null
contract.deleteRule: a slot that is not empty becomes empty; the active slot, if deleted, becomes none (autosave stops until the next save or load)
contract.autosaveRule: writes the active slot (last saved to or loaded) once the seconds since the last finished save (success or failure) or successful load reach autosaveIntervalSec; the count holds while any operation runs; one autosave per crossing; interval 0 or no active slot: never
contract.quickRule: F5 writes the quick slot, creating it when empty; F9 reads it; F9 on an empty quick slot: refused slot_empty, indicator nothing_to_load; on a corrupted one: refused slot_corrupted, indicator load_failed with the slot message; quickSlot null: both refused no_quick_slot, nothing shown
contract.busyRule: while an operation runs every request and both keys are refused busy (an unbound key stays unbound_key) and every row action is off; a due autosave waits

cases.note: The mirror of the case above (PL.slots-offset-mirror). There the +01:00 slot is the lower index, so a port that ignores the offset (10:00 reads as later) or flips its sign (11:00) still answers 0. Here the tie still goes to slot 0, and such a port answers 1.

cases.name: continue: the zone offset decides which slot is newer
cases.note: Slot 1 is 10:00Z, an hour after slot 0, though its clock reads 05:00. A port that ignores the offset reads 05:00Z and one that flips its sign reads 00:00Z, and both answer 0 (PL.slots-offset-mirror).

cases.note: Index 1 appears twice; its first entry (T1) counts, so slot 0 (T2) is the most recent.
